sentences.text: Neimongosaurus was a herbivorous theropod dinosaur belonging to the therizinosaurian group.
Researchers estimated the body length of Neimongosaurus to be between 2 and 3 meters, with Gregory S. Paul estimating the body mass to be 350 kg.
The lower jaw featured a toothless front region followed by five tooth sockets, though only one tooth was fully erupted in the known material.

The fossil record preserves seventeen vertebrae, including a tentative count of fourteen neck vertebrae that suggests one of the longest necks among non-bird dinosaurs, alongside twenty-two tail vertebrae indicating a relatively short tail.
The best-preserved upper arm bone measured 22.2 cm in length.
Its neck was tentatively counted at fourteen vertebrae, giving it one of the longest necks among non-bird dinosaurs.
Researchers suggest Neimongosaurus could extend its arms forward to reach and grasp vegetation.
The fossils were found in 1999 at a site called Sanhangobi, located 20 km southwest of Erenhot in Inner Mongolia.
The species was named Neimongosaurus yangi in 2001 by Zhang Xiaohong, Xu Xing, Paul Sereno, Kwang Xuewen, and Tan Lin, with the specific name honoring the paleontologist Yang Zhongjian.
A hole for blood vessels and nerves was located approximately 15 mm behind the front of the lower jaw.

Later studies placed Neimongosaurus within the family Therizinosauridae as a close relative of Segnosaurus, and a 2019 study grouped it with Erliansaurus, Suzhousaurus, and Therizinosaurus within that same family.
Fossils of Neimongosaurus come from the Iren Dabasu Formation in China, where the animal lived between 85.7 and 72.2 million years ago during the Santonian to Campanian stages.
